title: Night Shift
vision: The east wing groans above you.
A crack runs across the ceiling.
Concrete. Dust. Someone screaming your name.
wake: You jerk awake at the nurses’ desk. 20:04. Your shift has just begun, and the ceiling is still whole.

desk.text: “You were screaming in your sleep. What did you see?”

left.label: Tell her everything
left.after: She laughs. Then she looks up at the ceiling, just for a second.

right.label: “Just a bad dream”
right.after: She shrugs. The dream sits on your chest like a stone.

room-seven.text: Room 7. Blind for years. “You’re late, girl. Sit. I’ll tell you what kills you tonight.”

left.label: Sit and listen
left.after: “Water. Light. Iron.” She pats your hand. “In that order.”

right.label: Check her pills, leave
right.after: “As you like,” she says to the wall. “I’ve already buried you once.”

spill.text: A cleaner’s bucket has tipped over by the stairwell. The floor shines. The cleaner has gone home.
variants: A bucket has tipped over by the stairwell. The floor shines. Water, the old woman said.

left.label: Mop it up
left.after: Ten minutes on your knees. Your back hates you. The floor is dry.

right.label: Step around it
right.after: Not your job. You walk on, and the smell of bleach follows you.

supply.text: The lights flicker. One hand free, one shelf: A heavy flashlight, or the ward’s master keys.
variants: The lights flicker. Light, she said. But the ward’s master keys are on the same shelf, and you have one hand free.

left.label: Take the flashlight
left.after: Cold and heavy. You test it once. It works.

right.label: Take the keys
right.after: The ring jingles in your pocket. Nora raises an eyebrow: “Promoted?”

alarm.text: The alarm from the floor above. Mr. Wren’s oxygen. The elevator takes a minute he may not have.

left.label: Sprint up the stairs
left.after: You take the steps two at a time, past the spot you mopped.

right.label: Wait for the elevator
right.after: It stops between floors, shudders, then moves on. You stop breathing for a while.

tank.text: Mr. Wren breathes again. Behind his bed, a spare oxygen tank hisses softly. The gauge is in the red.

left.label: Haul it out now
left.after: It weighs more than you do. You drag it into the corridor and open a window.

right.label: Note it for morning
right.after: You write it on the chart. Someone will handle it. Someone always does.

east-wing.text: “Aris wants the old files from the east wing storeroom. Back in ten.”
variants: “Aris wants files from the east wing. Your east wing.” She tries to grin. “Back in ten?”

left.label: Go with her
left.after: “It’s files, not a war.” In the storeroom you both find a crack wider than your hand. She stops talking.

right.label: Let her go
right.after: Her footsteps fade down the east corridor. They take a long time to fade.

aris.text: “People say you’re scaring the ward. Is there something you need to tell me?”
variants: “People say you’re scaring the ward.” You’ve seen the crack. He hasn’t. “Well?”

left.label: “Clear the east wing”
left.after: His jaw tightens. “Bring me proof, or go home.” But he looks up too.

right.label: “I’m just tired”
right.after: “Then drink something.” He walks off under the ceiling you watched fall.

lamp.text: Mr. Wren’s reading lamp is spitting sparks at the socket. He’s asleep. The air smells faintly sweet.

left.label: Yank the plug
left.after: Snap. Dark. You stand there until your hands stop shaking.

right.label: Call maintenance
right.after: “At this hour?” says the phone. You stay until the sparks die on their own.

red-handle.text: Burning rubber, from somewhere below. The red handle is right there. A false alarm costs you your job tonight.

left.label: Pull it
left.after: Bells everywhere. People in pyjamas. Someone calls you crazy. They’re still walking out.

right.label: Check the basement
right.after: Stairs, dark, heat. A fuse box is smoking. By the time you’re back, nobody knows anything.

blackout.text: Every light dies at once. In the black, the elevator doors are grinding open somewhere close.
variants: Every light dies at once. Light, she said. Close by, the elevator doors are grinding open.

left.label: Keep walking
left.after: The beam finds it: An open shaft, one step ahead. You go around.

right.label: Wait for the generator
right.after: Four minutes in the dark. Something above you keeps shifting its weight.

halina.text: Room 7. Everyone has gone and she is still in her chair, smiling at nothing. “There you are.”

left.label: Carry her
left.after: She weighs nothing. She hums in your ear the whole way. “Iron,” she says, pleased.

right.label: Leave her
right.after: “Of course,” she calls after you. She keeps humming. You can hear it for two floors.

door.text: The building has shifted. The door to the inside stairs is jammed and locked.
variants: The building has shifted. The door to the inside stairs is jammed and locked. The master keys are in your pocket.

left.label: Go through it
left.after: The key turns on the second try. Concrete stairs. Solid. You run.

right.label: Take the fire escape
right.after: Outside, the cold hits you. The iron stairs are moving.

fire-escape.text: Old iron, five floors down, bolts weeping rust. Every landing sways in the wind.
variants: Old iron, five floors down, bolts weeping rust. Iron, she said. In that order.

left.label: Run for it
left.after: It shakes itself loose behind you. You jump the last flight.

right.label: Slowly, one at a time
right.after: Step. Wait. Step. Above you, a bolt lets go and falls past your face.

third-floor.text: You’re out. Cold grass. A torch is waving from the east wing, third floor. Nora. She’s still up there.

right.label: Scream at her to jump
right.after: You scream until your voice gives out. The torch stops moving.

slip.title: Wet Marble
slip.text: Your foot found the bleach before your eye did. The step was marble.
chain: You ran the stairs you never dried
Your foot went out from under you

shaft.title: One Step Ahead
shaft.text: The doors were open. The elevator wasn’t there.
chain: You left the flashlight on the shelf
You heard the doors and walked anyway
shaft.hint: You left the flashlight on the shelf. It looked great there.

spark.title: Sweet Air
spark.text: The room was on fire before you heard it.
chain: You saw the gauge in the red
For an hour the room filled with oxygen
spark.hint: You left a note for the morning. There is no morning.

frame.title: The Frame
frame.text: You put your shoulder into the door. The door was all that was holding up the wall.
chain: You chose the flashlight over the keys
frame.hint: Flashlights don’t open doors. Now you know.

iron.title: Old Iron
iron.text: Too much weight, too much hurry. The bolts had been waiting since 1962.
chain: You carried Halina out of Room 7
You kept Nora out of the east wing
The landing came away from the wall
iron.hint: You saved someone, congratulations. Now try doing it slowly.

vision.text: You reached the third floor. The ceiling came down exactly the way you remember it.
chain: You let Nora go alone at 22:20
She stayed in the east wing
You saw her torch from the lawn
vision.hint: “I’ll come with you” was free two hours ago.

panic.title: Which Way Out
panic.text: You stop in the corridor and can’t remember which way is out. Somebody is humming.
chain: You knew what was coming all night
You stopped trusting your own eyes
panic.hint: You saw the future and still couldn’t find the exit.

collapse.title: Double Shift
collapse.text: Your knees go. The floor is very comfortable. You’ll just stay a moment.
chain: You carried too much, too far
collapse.hint: You were going to be a hero. You fell asleep on the floor.

alone.title: Nobody Came
alone.text: You shout from under the plaster. The ward has heard you shout all night. Nobody comes.
chain: You frightened them once too often
alone.hint: You said all night it would fall. You were right. Nobody cares.

everyone.title: Everyone Out
everyone.text: 00:00. Nora on one side, Halina on the other. The east wing folds in on itself. Halina turns her blind face to you. “See? On time.”
everyone.hint: The best ending. Don’t worry, there are plenty of ways to die.

two-on-the-grass.title: Two on the Grass
two-on-the-grass.text: 00:00. The east wing falls with a sound you already know. Nora’s hand is crushing yours.
two-on-the-grass.hint: You’re both fine. How’s Room 7 doing?

survivor.title: Alone on the Lawn
survivor.text: 00:00. You’re alive. You don’t look at the third floor.
survivor.hint: You’re alive. You’ll never tell anyone how.
